column3: It supplies the nearest contrast: those kept away from the Fire do not hear its sound, whereas the focus describes those inside it.
Thrown hearing joined to falsehood offers only a distant antecedent to the focus's failed hearing.
It directly locates the wretched in the Fire with exhalation and inhalation, closely clarifying the focus's exhalation there.
Its absence of vain speech and falsehood in the other final abode forms a meaningful contrast to the focus's closed hearing in the Fire.
The nearby promise that faithful good work is recorded supplies a limited righteous counterpart to the condemned scene.
It distinguishes physical listening from understanding, providing a worldly counterpart to the focus's inability to hear.
The peaceful abode's freedom from vain speech contrasts with the focus's punitive auditory closure.
It begins the immediate apocalyptic movement that leads into the focus's Fire scene, but adds no hearing detail.
Listening to lies supplies a distant misuse of hearing, not the final condition described in the focus.
The other abode's absence of vain and sinful speech gives a secondary contrast to the Fire's silence toward its inhabitants.
It immediately identifies the worshippers and their objects as fuel entering Hell, which the focus then depicts from within.
The divine attribute of hearing offers only a broad contrast to the inhabitants' inability to hear.
It joins hearing with the Fire's rage and exhalation before arrival, usefully contrasting its audible menace with the focus's internal closure.
Seeking refuge with the All-Hearing does not materially clarify hearing inside the Fire.
Reduced hearing without understanding offers a remote worldly analogy to the focus's deprivation.
The contrast between claiming to hear and truly hearing gives a moral precursor to the focus's final non-hearing.
Its irreversible destruction and non-return extend the immediate judgment sequence before the focus.
It describes hearing that cannot reach comprehension because of covered hearts and burdened ears, a close antecedent pattern.
The inability of false gods to help does not add to the focus's auditory condition.
It is the immediately preceding statement that all the condemned enter and remain in the Fire the focus describes.
Dismissing the recited signs after hearing them is a distant antecedent to the final loss of hearing.
The brief rebuke for disbelief adds no distinct understanding of the Fire scene.
Unwearied worship in heaven is only a broad contrast to the focus's condemned inhabitants.
Listening to lies alongside outward but unreal belief supplies a remote failed-reception parallel.
Eternal residence in gardens gives only a general contrary final abode.
The immediately preceding vision of the wrongdoers' shocked recognition frames the judgment that reaches the focus.
Humiliation and expulsion in the Solomon narrative do not clarify the focus.
It immediately separates those kept far from the Fire from the inhabitants in the focus, completing the contrast initiated by 21:102.
The command not to speak in Hell provides a complementary image of communication closed off within the Fire.
Worldly respite and territorial decline do not materially illuminate the focus.
Disputation while in the Fire is a limited counterpoint to the focus's inability to hear there.
Pride and refuge from disputation do not add to the particular Fire condition.
The Fire scorching their faces supplies a concrete neighboring depiction of bodily suffering in the abode.
Protection from the greatest terror offers a local opposite outcome, but is less direct than the Fire contrasts already listed.
Those cast into the Fire hear its roaring exhalation, a close auditory contrast to the focus's no-hearing within it.
Division and return to God do not clarify the Fire's exhalation or auditory closure.
Turning away so as not to hear provides a distant worldly antecedent to the focus's non-hearing.
The cosmic folding and re-creation give judgment context but no particular link to the focus's condition.
Sudden arrival without awareness does not clarify hearing or the Fire scene.
The earth's stabilizing mountains and paths do not add to the focus.
The worldly payment of works does not illuminate the final Fire condition.
The accusation of fabrication does not add to the focus beyond a remote false-speech resonance.
Exclusion from hearing the highest assembly gives a distant structural parallel of barred hearing.
The righteous inheriting the earth offers a local contrast to the wrongdoers' final fate.
The question whether invoked objects can hear connects false worship to the condemned worshippers and their objects in the nearby sequence.
Admission to gardens for those who endure gives a general contrary outcome, without clarifying the focus's auditory state.
Sealed hearts resulting in non-hearing offer a remote moral antecedent to punitive non-hearing.
The surah's declaration of a message for worshippers supplies only broad local context.
The inhabitants cry out in the Fire for release, adding a complementary picture of futile sound and response there.
Hearing the call, believing, and seeking forgiveness presents the responsive alternative to the focus's closed hearing.
Hearing God's speech and then distorting it is a distant misuse of reception.
Mercy for the worlds is a broad local contrast, not an explanation of this punishment.
It makes the failure to hear a failure of hearts rather than ears, illuminating the moral dimension of non-hearing.
The warning function of the Criterion offers only general context for those facing punishment.
Those unable to understand, see, or hear are assigned to Hell, directly connecting failed hearing with the focus's destination.
The summons to submit to one God is a local antecedent but does not add to the Fire condition.
The call to hear a believer presents a minimal contrary instance of receptive response.
The Day's restricted speech and division into wretched and happy people extend the eschatological setting of the focus.
The call to heed destroyed generations offers a distant warning through hearing.
The warning of an unknown, possibly near fulfillment is only broad local judgment context.
The inability of alleged partners to hear reinforces the false-worship setting of the immediate Fire passage.
Refusal to answer the call to worship leads to entering Hell humiliated, linking rejected address with the focus's fate.
The severe punishment of persistent disbelief gives a general final-judgment parallel.
God's knowledge of open and hidden speech is only a distant contrast to the inhabitants' hearing.
Professing hearing while disobeying supplies a remote antecedent to failed reception.
Gardens and palaces promised to the messenger do not clarify the focus.
The command to listen and the warning of painful punishment offer only a general hearing-and-punishment pairing.
The possibility of a temporary trial does not add to the Fire's inner condition.
The sealing of hearing and hearts with a great punishment directly supplies a pre-final pattern for the focus's non-hearing.
The final appeal for just judgment gives only broad closure to the surah's warning.
Regret at the sudden Hour does not clarify exhalation or inability to hear.
Punishment for obstruction and failure to recognize the pious gives only general judgment context.
Guidance and schism, followed by God's hearing, do not materially illuminate the focus.
The statement that God is Hearing and Knowing adds no specific connection after broader divine-hearing parallels.
Death, restoration, and divine bounty do not clarify the focus.
The threatened removal of hearing supplies a limited pre-final counterpart to the focus's deprivation.
Saying they heard while disobeying repeats the failed-response pattern without adding much beyond earlier cards.
The heard blasphemous speech followed by the punishment of burning gives a distant speech-to-Fire consequence.
The divine attribute of hearing in a divorce ruling does not add to the focus.
The divine attribute of hearing in a command to fight does not clarify the focus.
The divine attribute of hearing in battle arrangements does not clarify the focus.
Hearing abuse during trial does not materially illuminate the final Fire condition.
The bare divine names Hearing and Knowing add no distinct value.
The divine attribute of hearing in an oath instruction does not clarify the focus.
Faith and the divine attribute of hearing do not materially illuminate the focus.
A prayer answered by the Hearer of prayer does not clarify the Fire scene.
Liability for altering a bequest and the divine attribute of hearing do not add to the focus.
A prayer for acceptance during building does not illuminate the focus.
The believers' statement that they hear and obey presents a concise opposite to failed hearing, though it is redundant here.
Justice commands and divine hearing do not clarify the focus.
Signs for people who hear do not materially add to the final Fire condition.
False intercessory worship and divine judgment provide a distant counterpart to the condemned worshippers in the focus's sequence.
Great punishment in the Hereafter offers only a general, non-specific judgment parallel.
A pleasant life does not clarify the focus beyond a generic contrary outcome.
A lofty garden is a minimal contrary final-abode image.
The regulations of nursing do not add to the focus.
Revelation, warning, and belief in the Hereafter offer only broad antecedent context.
Demanding direct divine speech is a distant contrast to receptive hearing of revelation.
The command to glorify the Lord does not clarify the focus.
Prayer, charity, and forgiveness do not materially illuminate the Fire's exhalation and non-hearing.
It gives the immediate local Fire threat that the disbelievers cannot ward from their faces or backs, directly framing the focus's internal scene.
The people of the Fire call to the people of the Garden for water and provision, providing an essential parallel of futile address across the final divide.
The people in the Fire appeal to its keepers to ask their Lord for relief, directly extending the focus's closed and suffering communication setting.
The keepers answer the Fire's inhabitants by recalling the messengers and leaving them to their unanswered prayer, completing the exchange begun in 40:49.
The criminals call to the keeper of Hell for an end, but are told they will remain, a direct picture of unrelieved speech within the Fire.
Those who disbelieve are driven to Hell in groups and meet its keepers at the opened gates, supplying the entry scene before the focus's condition inside.
The command to enter Hell's gates and remain there directly complements the focus's location and continuing condition in it.
Those destined for the Fire are returned to it whenever they seek to leave, adding the inescapability of the abode in the focus.
Those gathered blind, mute, and deaf are placed in Hell, whose blaze is increased when it subsides; it closely joins sensory deprivation and Fire.
Being thrown bound into a narrow place of Hell and calling for destruction gives a compressed counterpart of distress within the enclosure.
Hell is promised to all those who follow error, supplying the wider destination behind the focus's condemned group.
Hell's seven gates and allotted groups add a structural account of entry and division within the destination.
Beds and coverings of Fire give a bodily image of being enclosed in the punishment described by the focus.
Hell lies before the tyrant, followed by unbearable drinking, extending the focus's bodily suffering in the Fire.
Those whose scales are light are in Hell eternally, supplying the judgment criterion for the Fire scene that 23:104 further depicts.
The command to enter Hell because of prior disbelief gives a concise causal counterpart to the focus's state inside it.
The disbelievers remain in the Fire without death or reduced punishment, reinforcing the focus's unrelieved duration.
The condemned are driven forcefully toward the Fire of Hell, providing a transition into the destination the focus depicts.
The guilty are dragged on their faces into the Fire and told to taste its touch, adding a direct sensory punishment parallel.
The command to expose the condemned person to Hell supplies a direct transition into the place named by the focus.
The blazing Fire strips away the extremities, offering a closely related bodily account of its violence.
Hell is presented as a place lying in wait for transgressors, framing the destination of the focus's inhabitants.
Its inhabitants taste neither coolness nor drink, extending the focus's description of comprehensive sensory deprivation.
The blazing Fire is made visible to whoever sees, offering an external contrast to the focus's interior auditory closure.
The kindled Fire of God supplies a concentrated description of the Fire's active force around the focus's suffering.
The Fire is closed over its inhabitants, a strong enclosure image that complements the focus's closed communication setting.
The condemned person will enter a Fire of flame, giving a concise direct destination parallel.
